workflow_summary: The developer wants an agent that proactively notifies customers about their orders — e.g. "order confirmed / paid", "shipped with tracking", "out for delivery", "delayed", "delivered", "cancelled/refunded". That decomposes into: (a) getting order and fulfillment state changes out of the commerce platform, (b) enriching shipped orders with normalized carrier tracking status, (c) delivering the message on email, (d) delivering it on SMS/WhatsApp, and (e) templating the message plus tracking whether it actually landed (opens, bounces, delivery receipts). No user was available to answer clarifying questions, so this report covers the two most common order sources (Shopify, WooCommerce) and both email and SMS/WhatsApp channels; the actual platform, channel mix, and region are recorded as open questions.

tasks.task_description: Retrieve order/shipment data and detect status changes from the store's commerce platform (webhooks + order lookup).

recommended_apis.rationale: Shopify emits webhook topics that map one-to-one onto the customer-facing milestones the agent needs (paid, fulfilled, partially fulfilled, cancelled, fulfillment created/updated, on-hold/released, ready for pickup), so the agent gets a precise trigger instead of having to diff order records. The Order object then supplies everything a message needs in one query (order name, email, phone, fulfillment/financial status, shipping address, statusPageUrl, canNotifyCustomer).
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: Webhook subscriptions: declare topics in the app config TOML ([[webhooks.subscriptions]] with topics + uri, including pubsub:// targets) or create shop-specific ones with the GraphQL Admin mutation webhookSubscriptionCreate. Relevant topics: orders/create, orders/paid, orders/updated, orders/fulfilled, orders/partially_fulfilled, orders/cancelled, fulfillments/create, fulfillments/update, fulfillment_orders/placed_on_hold, fulfillment_orders/hold_released, fulfillment_orders/line_items_prepared_for_pickup, fulfillment_orders/rescheduled. Order read: GraphQL Admin `order`/`orders` query selecting name, email, phone, displayFulfillmentStatus, displayFinancialStatus, fulfillments, fulfillmentOrders, shippingAddress, statusPageUrl, canNotifyCustomer.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Requires an app install with the `orders` scope (and `fulfillments`/`*_fulfillment_orders` for shipment topics); customer email/phone are protected customer data, which for App Store apps needs approval and data-handling commitments. Some topics are approval-gated/Plus-only (e.g. audit_events). Shopify itself already sends order confirmation and shipping notification emails, so the agent risks duplicate notifications unless store notifications are disabled or the agent restricts itself to milestones Shopify doesn't cover. GraphQL cost-based rate limiting and webhook retry/duplicate delivery must be handled (idempotency on webhook id).
open_questions: Is the store actually on Shopify? (unconfirmed — no user answer available.)
Exact HMAC verification header/retry policy for Shopify webhooks was not re-verified on this pass.
Whether the merchant will disable Shopify's built-in customer notifications to avoid double-messaging.

recommended_apis.rationale: The right choice for self-hosted WordPress stores: simple key/secret auth, an /orders resource with the full order payload, and webhook CRUD from the same API. It is weaker than Shopify for this workflow because there are no per-status topics — only order.created/updated/deleted — so the agent must persist previous status and diff it, and webhook delivery reliability depends on the store's wp-cron.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: GET /wp-json/wc/v3/orders (and /orders/{id}) with status/date filters, per_page/page pagination and X-WP-Total headers, for the polling fallback and enrichment. POST/GET/PUT/DELETE /wp-json/wc/v3/webhooks (plus /webhooks/batch) with {name, topic: order.created|order.updated|order.deleted, delivery_url, secret, status}; delivery logs readable per webhook. Webhook requests carry X-WC-Webhook-Topic/-Resource/-Event and X-WC-Webhook-Signature (base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the body).
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Auth is consumer key/secret over HTTP Basic and some hosts strip the Authorization header (documented query-string workaround) — a credential-leak footgun. Delivery is via wp_remote_post on wp-cron in the background, only the 25 most recent delivery logs are kept, and after 5 consecutive non-2xx responses the webhook is auto-disabled and must be re-enabled through the API, so the agent needs health monitoring plus a polling fallback. order.updated fires on many hooks, so duplicate/noisy events are expected and status diffing plus idempotency keys are mandatory.
open_questions: No documented retry/backoff for a single failed delivery was found beyond the 5-strike disable rule.
Whether shipment tracking numbers are available in the order payload depends on which tracking plugin the store uses (not part of core WooCommerce).

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Expose read/derive tools, not order mutations. Suggested tools: `list_recent_order_events(since, statuses[])` (normalizes Shopify webhook topics and WooCommerce order.updated diffs into one internal event vocabulary: created, paid, fulfilled, partially_fulfilled, out_for_delivery, delivered, delayed, cancelled, refunded); `get_order(order_id)` returning a normalized order view (order number, customer name, contact email/phone, line items, status, shipping address, tracking numbers+carriers, customer-facing status URL); `get_order_notification_state(order_id)` returning which updates were already sent (dedupe ledger). Webhook registration should be an operator/deployment concern, not an agent tool — at most expose read-only `list_webhook_subscriptions` and `get_webhook_health` (useful for WooCommerce's auto-disable behaviour). Do NOT expose order write/cancel/refund/fulfil mutations, webhook delete, or raw GraphQL passthrough; and have `get_order` return only the contact fields needed for messaging so customer PII is not spread across the agent context.

tasks.task_description: Get normalized carrier tracking status updates for shipped orders (in transit, out for delivery, exception/delay, delivered).

recommended_apis.rationale: Cheapest and simplest way to turn a tracking number into a normalized, push-updated status stream. The status/status_detail enums map almost directly onto customer-facing message types (out_for_delivery, delivery_exception, delayed, held, lost, return_to_sender, delivered), it includes est_delivery_date and a hosted public tracking URL you can put in the message, and there are canned test tracking codes for every state, which makes the agent easy to test end-to-end.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST /v2/trackers {tracker: {tracking_code, carrier}} to start tracking a label bought elsewhere (carrier auto-detected if omitted, but passing it is recommended); GET /v2/trackers/:id and GET /v2/trackers to read; each Tracker exposes status, status_detail, est_delivery_date, tracking_details[] history with locations, carrier_detail (service, guaranteed_delivery_date, initial_delivery_attempt) and public_url. Updates arrive as webhook Events when webhooks are enabled. Auth: HTTP Basic with the API key as the username.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: $0.01–$0.03 per tracked shipment (Advanced Tracking with branded pages/notifications is $0.03), so cost scales with order volume. Trackers are immutable — you cannot attach the order id later, so store your own tracker_id → order_id mapping (or use it at creation time). Tracking codes are not globally unique and duplicate create calls within 3 months return the original tracker, which can silently cross-wire two orders. Some carriers restrict third-party tracking and may require carrier-specific credentials.
open_questions: Whether EasyPost webhook Events can be registered via API vs dashboard was not verified on this pass.
Whether the retention window of tracking_details is long enough for post-delivery support queries.

recommended_apis.rationale: Richer post-purchase feature set for the same job: 1000+ courier coverage with slug detection, an AI estimated-delivery-date with a confidence code, on_time_status, and a webhook payload that already contains order_number and a branded tracking URL — which reduces how much joining the agent must do. It is a heavier, more product-shaped platform than EasyPost and its webhook configuration is dashboard-only.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST /tracking/{version}/trackings {tracking_number, slug|slug_group, order_number, custom_fields} on base https://api.aftership.com with an `as-api-key` header; GET/PUT/DELETE /trackings/{id}; POST retrack and mark-as-completed; POST detect courier; GET couriers (to learn per-courier mandatory fields); Estimated Delivery Date prediction (single + batch). Inbound: `tracking_update` webhook with tag/subtag, checkpoints[], aftership_estimated_delivery_date, courier_tracking_link, verified by the aftership-hmac-sha256 header.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Webhook URLs and the webhook secret are configured in the AfterShip admin portal rather than via API, so provisioning is manual and cannot be automated by the agent. Date-versioned API (e.g. 2026-07) means you must pin and periodically migrate versions. Courier auto-detection depends on the account's Preferred Courier List being configured, and some couriers require extra mandatory fields or creation fails. Pricing was not inspected — AfterShip is quota/shipment based and materially more expensive than raw EasyPost tracking at low volume.
open_questions: AfterShip pricing tiers and included shipment quotas were not fetched — verify cost per tracked shipment before committing.
Rate limits (there is a dedicated Rate Limit doc page) were not inspected.

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Two tools: `start_tracking(order_id, tracking_number, carrier?)` (idempotent — must look up an existing tracker for the same code+carrier before creating one, because both providers dedupe silently) and `get_tracking_status(order_id|tracking_number)` returning a provider-agnostic shape {state, state_detail, eta, last_scan{time,location,message}, public_tracking_url, is_exception}. Normalize EasyPost's status/status_detail and AfterShip's tag/subtag into one internal enum so the message templates never branch on vendor vocabulary. Tracking-provider webhooks should be ingested by the server and surfaced as events, not exposed as an agent-callable tool. Do NOT expose tracker delete, 'retrack', or mark-as-completed (state-mutating and billable), and do not expose label-buying/insurance endpoints from the same EasyPost key — scope the key to tracking only.

tasks.task_description: Send the order update to the customer over email.

recommended_apis.rationale: Purpose-built for transactional mail, which is exactly what order updates are: one call sends a stored template with a data model, Metadata lets you stamp the order id onto the message for later reconciliation, and Message Streams enforce separation between transactional and marketing traffic (important for deliverability and for not letting an agent accidentally send bulk mail on the transactional stream). Batch endpoint covers backfills.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST https://api.postmarkapp.com/email/withTemplate with {TemplateAlias|TemplateId, TemplateModel, From, To, Tag, Metadata, TrackOpens, TrackLinks, MessageStream}; POST /email/batchWithTemplates for up to 500 messages per call; auth via the X-Postmark-Server-Token header. Plain POST /email exists for non-templated sends.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Pricing has a hard cliff: free tier is 100 emails/month with no overages, and the next tier starts at 10,000 emails/month ($15–$18/mo, overage $1.20–$1.80 per 1,000) — nothing in between. The From address must be a confirmed Sender Signature (domain DKIM/SPF setup required before production). Default activity/content retention is 45 days (longer retention is a paid add-on), so long-term audit of what was sent must live in your own datastore. Max 100 templates per server.
open_questions: Per-second/per-minute API rate limits were not confirmed on the pages inspected.
Whether the merchant already has a domain authenticated with another ESP (would change the migration cost).

recommended_apis.rationale: A strong alternative, especially if SMS is also going through Twilio (one vendor, one billing relationship). Its personalizations array (up to 1000 recipients per request) and Handlebars dynamic templates handle both single order updates and bulk catch-up sends, and custom_args carry the order id into event data. Slightly more complex payload shape and a broader marketing surface than the workflow needs.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST https://api.sendgrid.com/v3/mail/send (EU subusers: https://api.eu.sendgrid.com) with Authorization: Bearer <API key>; body has personalizations[] (to/cc/bcc, subject, dynamic_template_data, custom_args, send_at), from, reply_to, content[], attachments[], template_id ('d-' prefixed for dynamic templates), categories (max 10), batch_id, send_at (max 72h ahead).
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: From address must be a verified sender / authenticated domain. EU regional sending requires a Pro plan or above plus an EU IP and EU subuser — a real constraint if customer data must stay in the EU. Scheduling is capped at 72 hours ahead. The same API key can reach marketing features, so scope API key permissions tightly. Deliverability on shared IPs is more variable than Postmark's transactional-only reputation (vendor-comparison claim, not independently verified).
open_questions: Current SendGrid pricing tiers/free-tier volume were not fetched.
Whether an order-update sender should use a dedicated IP at the merchant's volume.

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Expose a single high-level tool `send_order_email(order_id, update_type, channel_overrides?)` rather than a generic `send_email(to, subject, html)`. The MCP server should resolve the recipient address itself from the order record (never accept a free-text `to` from the model), pick the template alias from `update_type`, build the merge model from normalized order + tracking data, stamp Metadata/custom_args with {order_id, update_type, idempotency_key}, and refuse to send if the ledger already recorded that (order_id, update_type). Also expose read-only `list_email_templates()` so the agent can discover which update types are supported. Do NOT expose template create/edit/delete, suppression deletion (un-suppressing a bounced or complained recipient is a compliance risk), attachment upload, batch sends to arbitrary recipient lists, or the marketing/broadcast stream.

tasks.task_description: Send the order update over SMS and/or WhatsApp (and note push as an unresolved channel).

recommended_apis.api_name: Twilio Programmable Messaging (+ WhatsApp Content Templates)
recommended_apis.rationale: One Message resource covers SMS, MMS and WhatsApp (channel address form whatsapp:+1555...), so the agent has a single send path with a single status vocabulary across channels, and Messaging Services add scheduling and link shortening (useful for tracking URLs in a 160-char SMS). Content Templates are omnichannel, so the same approved template can be reused across WhatsApp and SMS.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: Create a Message (POST to the Messages resource) with To/From (E.164, alphanumeric sender, short code, or whatsapp: channel address) or MessagingServiceSid, plus Body — or ContentSid (HX...) + ContentVariables for approved templates; Fetch/Read Messages for status, error_code, price; Update Message to redact body/To; Media and MessageFeedback sub-resources. Outbound status values: accepted, scheduled, queued, sending, sent, delivered, undelivered, failed, canceled, and read (WhatsApp/RCS).
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Heavy onboarding before the first production message: US SMS from a 10DLC number requires A2P Brand + Campaign registration (Tax ID for Standard brands, opt-in/opt-out/HELP language, daily caps by brand type/Trust Score, extra carrier fees and filtering if unregistered); WhatsApp needs a WhatsApp Business Account and Meta-approved templates that cannot be edited after submission, can only be sent outside the 24-hour customer service window as templates, may be paused (3h/6h) or deactivated on negative feedback, and deleted template names are blocked for 30 days. Message bodies are PII (30-day retention marker) and per-message cost is real, so retries must be bounded.
open_questions: Which channels the merchant actually wants (email only vs +SMS vs +WhatsApp) — the clarifying question could not be answered.
Where the customer's SMS/WhatsApp consent is stored; neither Shopify nor WooCommerce consent state was researched.
Per-country SMS pricing and whether an alphanumeric sender ID is usable in the merchant's markets.

recommended_apis.rationale: Credible single-API alternative covering SMS, MMS, RCS, WhatsApp, Messenger, Viber and Email, with documented cross-channel failover (e.g. try WhatsApp, fall back to SMS) — attractive for order updates where reachability matters more than channel. It also ships a WhatsApp Template Management API (template lifecycle via API rather than console) and a 10DLC API for US registration.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: Messages API send endpoint (per-channel message bodies) authenticated with JWT signed by an application private key; companion references: WhatsApp Template Management API, External Accounts API, 10DLC API, Channel Manager. A hosted sandbox exists for WhatsApp/Viber testing before production senders are approved.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: JWT-per-request auth (application ID + private key) is more setup than a static API key. The same US A2P 10DLC and Meta WhatsApp template-approval requirements apply — the provider does not remove them. Only the overview page was inspected: exact request/response schemas, delivery-receipt webhook payloads and pricing were not verified, so treat implementation details as unconfirmed.
open_questions: Exact send payload and delivery-receipt (DLR) webhook schema per channel not verified.
Vonage pricing for SMS/WhatsApp in the merchant's target countries not checked.
Whether Vonage's channel failover is billable per attempted channel.

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Expose `send_order_sms(order_id, update_type)` and `send_order_whatsapp(order_id, update_type)` — or better, one `notify_customer(order_id, update_type, channels[])` that the server fans out — with the recipient number resolved server-side from the order and a mandatory consent check (skip and report 'no_consent' rather than sending). For WhatsApp the tool must accept only a known template key mapped to an approved ContentSid plus a variables map; never let the model compose free-form WhatsApp body text for business-initiated messages. Enforce an idempotency ledger, a per-order rate cap (e.g. max N updates/day), and quiet-hours handling. Do NOT expose: template submission/deletion, A2P brand/campaign registration, phone-number purchase, message redaction/delete, or arbitrary `to` numbers. Push notifications (APNs/FCM/OneSignal) were not researched — treat as an open channel that would need its own tool and device-token store.

tasks.task_description: Render/manage message templates and track delivery outcomes (opens, bounces, complaints, delivery receipts) so the agent knows whether the customer was actually reached.

recommended_apis.rationale: Gives the most complete closed loop for email: server-side templates with a validate endpoint (so template changes can be CI-checked), event webhooks for delivery/bounce/open/click/spam-complaint/subscription-change, a Messages API for searching outbound messages and per-message opens/clicks, and automatic suppression management so a bounced customer isn't hammered by every subsequent order update.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: Templates: create/edit/get/list/delete/validate, push templates between servers (limit 100 per server). Webhooks API: list/create/edit/delete webhooks for Delivery, Bounce, Open, Click, SpamComplaint, SubscriptionChange. Messages API: outbound message search, message details/dump, message opens, opens for a single message, clicks. Suppressions API: dump/create/delete suppressions. Stats API for aggregate bounce/open/click counts.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Message content/activity retention defaults to 45 days (custom retention is a paid add-on on Pro+), so the agent's own audit trail must be persisted locally. 100-template-per-server cap limits a 'template per update type per locale' explosion. Open tracking is unreliable by nature (image blocking) and should not be treated as proof of delivery. Webhook endpoints must be secured (Postmark documents protecting the endpoint) and events can arrive out of order.
open_questions: Whether Postmark webhook signing (vs basic-auth-protected URL) is available was not verified.
Retention add-on pricing beyond 'starts at $5/month' not itemized per volume.

recommended_apis.api_name: Twilio SendGrid (Dynamic Templates + Event Webhook) and Twilio Messaging status
recommended_apis.rationale: If both channels run on Twilio, one vendor covers both loops: SendGrid dynamic templates (Handlebars) with categories/custom_args carried into activity data for email, and Message resource status/error_code (plus status callbacks) for SMS/WhatsApp delivery receipts including WhatsApp 'read'. Slightly less coherent than Postmark for email-only setups, and the SMS and email event models are separate.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: Email: template_id ('d-' dynamic) + dynamic_template_data on POST /v3/mail/send; categories and custom_args flow into activity/event data. SMS/WhatsApp: Fetch a Message / Read multiple Messages for status, error_code, error_message, price; Update Message to redact body/To.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Two different event pipelines and two different status vocabularies to normalize. The SendGrid Event Webhook and the Twilio StatusCallback mechanism were not inspected in this pass, so their payloads and signature verification are unverified. Reading message status by polling costs API calls and is race-prone; callbacks are the correct pattern. Twilio message bodies carry PII retention implications.
open_questions: SendGrid Event Webhook payload/signature verification not verified.
Twilio StatusCallback parameter list not verified (the docs URL tried returned 404) — confirm before relying on it.
Whether SendGrid template versions can be managed via API in the plan the merchant would buy.

recommended_apis.rationale: A different architecture worth considering: instead of the agent rendering and sending messages, it posts normalized 'Order Shipped'/'Order Delayed' events with a profile, and Klaviyo flows own the templates, channel choice, consent and reporting. This minimizes the agent's messaging surface and reuses the merchant's existing marketing stack, at the cost of losing per-message control and adding a heavier dependency.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST https://a.klaviyo.com/api/events with JSON:API body {data:{type:'event', attributes:{metric, profile, properties, backfill}}}, Authorization header, accept/content-type application/vnd.api+json, and a mandatory dated `revision` header (e.g. 2026-07-15).
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Only the event-creation reference was inspected; the rest of the loop (flow triggering, template management, delivery/bounce reporting endpoints, SMS consent handling, pricing by active profiles) is unverified. Dated `revision` header means scheduled version migrations, and several older revisions are already marked deprecated. Delivery is asynchronous and indirect: the agent cannot easily assert 'this customer was notified' from the API response alone.
open_questions: How to read per-message delivery/bounce outcomes back from Klaviyo was not researched.
Klaviyo pricing model and whether transactional order updates are permitted alongside marketing consent rules.
Whether flow-based delivery gives sufficient timing determinism for 'out for delivery' style updates.

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Expose `list_templates()` (read-only, so the agent can only choose from vetted update types), `render_preview(update_type, order_id)` (renders without sending — the safe way to let a human or the agent verify copy), and `get_delivery_outcome(order_id, update_type)` returning a normalized {state: queued|sent|delivered|opened|bounced|complained|undelivered, provider_message_id, error}. The MCP server should ingest provider webhooks (Postmark delivery/bounce/spam-complaint, SendGrid events, Twilio status callbacks) into its own ledger and answer from that ledger, rather than proxying provider event APIs. Do NOT expose template create/edit/delete, suppression deletion, message redaction/deletion, or raw stats dumps of other customers' messages; and never expose an 'un-suppress and resend' capability — repeated sending to a hard-bounced or complaining recipient is the fastest way to lose sending reputation.

cross_task_notes:
Recommended overall MCP server layout: one server with four internal adapters (commerce, tracking, email, messaging) and a small state store of its own. Suggested tool surface: list_recent_order_events, get_order, start_tracking, get_tracking_status, list_templates, render_preview, notify_customer(order_id, update_type, channels[]), get_delivery_outcome, get_order_notification_state. The natural composition is: order/fulfillment webhook → get_order → start_tracking (on first fulfillment) → tracking webhook → get_tracking_status → notify_customer → get_delivery_outcome, with every step keyed by (order_id, update_type) in an idempotency ledger.

Cross-cutting realities that dominate this workflow more than API choice does:
1) Duplicate suppression. Shopify orders/updated and WooCommerce order.updated both fire on many unrelated changes, and webhooks can be redelivered; the ledger, not the model's judgment, must decide whether a message was already sent.
2) Consent and compliance. Email needs an authenticated sending domain and honoured suppressions; US SMS needs A2P 10DLC brand+campaign registration with opt-in/opt-out/HELP language; WhatsApp needs a WABA and Meta-approved templates and only allows free-form text inside a 24-hour customer service window. None of these can be automated away by the agent, and the MCP server should hard-fail rather than send when consent or template approval is missing.
3) Cost per action. Tracking is ~$0.01–$0.03 per shipment, SMS/WhatsApp are per-message, email is per-1,000. Every send tool should be treated as an expensive, non-idempotent side effect: bounded retries, per-order caps, no agent-initiated bulk sends.
4) Auth spread. Shopify OAuth access token + scopes, WooCommerce consumer key/secret over Basic, EasyPost Basic-with-API-key, AfterShip as-api-key, Postmark X-Postmark-Server-Token, SendGrid bearer key, Twilio account SID/auth token, Vonage JWT, Klaviyo key + dated revision header. Keep each credential in the server (never in tool arguments) and scope keys narrowly (e.g. an EasyPost key limited to tracking, a SendGrid key without marketing scopes).
5) PII minimization. Order payloads contain protected customer data (Shopify explicitly gates it) and message bodies are PII at Twilio. Tools should return only the fields needed to compose the message, and the agent should never receive full customer lists.
6) Unresolved decisions the developer must make (the clarifying question went unanswered in this non-interactive run): actual commerce platform, channel mix (email only vs +SMS vs +WhatsApp vs push), region/data-residency (affects SendGrid EU plan and GDPR posture), volume (affects Postmark's 100→10,000 pricing cliff and 10DLC brand tier), and whether Shopify/WooCommerce built-in customer emails will be disabled to avoid double-notifying customers. Push notifications were not researched at all and remain an open gap."
